settings_policy.scope: A starting point for future I Am Free to Dream recordings. Language and arrangement overrides preserve local musical choices; historical actual settings remain unchanged.

defaults.vocal_gender: Unselected; voice directed in the language prompt
defaults.exclude_styles: EDM, heavy dance beats, aggressive percussion, theatrical belting, excessive vocal runs, vocoder, chopped vocals

settings_policy.exception_rule: Inherit baseline, then adopted language overrides, then adopted language/arrangement overrides. Document changed controls, musical reason, decision reference and review status. Proposed comparisons do not apply automatically. Per-run author directions take precedence and must be recorded. This policy does not authorize generation credits.

entries.title: ମତେ ସପନ୍ ଦେଖ୍‌ବାକେ ମନା ନାଇଁ — Playful Sambalpuri Duet
entries.lyrics:
[Intro - Male Lead, Soft Female Responses]
ମତେ ସପନ୍ ଦେଖ୍‌ବାକେ ମନା ନାଇଁ,
ମଝି ବାଟେ ହଜିଯିବାକେ ବି ମନା ନାଇଁ।
ଧ୍ରୁବତାରା ବାଟ୍ ଦେଖେଇଦେବା।

[Verse 1 - Male Lead, Playful Female Answers]
ସାଉଁଟି... ସାଉଁଟି...
ସଂସାର୍‌କେ ଜାବ୍‌ଡ଼ି ଧରିଛେଁ—
ଜୁଡ଼ିଦେବାର୍ ଆଶାନେ,
ସଜେଇଦେବାର୍ ଆଶାନେ।

[Verse 2 - Male Lead, Gentle Female Harmony]
କୁମ୍ଭାର୍ ମୁଇଁ।

ଗଢ଼ିଦେବାର୍ ସିଖିଛେଁ,
ରଙ୍ଗ୍ ଲଗେଇ,
ତୋର୍ ମୁହେଁ ହସ୍ ବୁନ୍‌ବାର୍ ସିଖିଛେଁ।

[Chorus - Male Lead, Warm Female Replies]
ମତେ ସପନ୍ ଦେଖ୍‌ବାକେ ମନା ନାଇଁ,
ମଝି ବାଟେ ହଜିଯିବାକେ ବି ମନା ନାଇଁ।
ଧ୍ରୁବତାରା ବାଟ୍ ଦେଖେଇଦେବା।

[Bridge - Female Solo, Joyful Invitation]
ଆ, ପାହାଡ଼୍ ଚଢ଼୍‌ମା।
ଆ, ଜନ୍ ଦେଖ୍‌ମା।
ବାଦଲ୍ ସାଙ୍ଗେ କାନ୍ଧ୍ ମିଲେଇ,
ବର୍ଷା ହେଇ ଝର୍‌ବାର୍ ମନ୍ତର୍ ସିଖ୍‌ମା।

[Final Chorus - Male and Female Duet]
ମତେ ସପନ୍ ଦେଖ୍‌ବାକେ ମନା ନାଇଁ।
ତୋର୍ ସପନ୍‌କେ ମୋର୍ ସପନ୍‌ନେ
ଗୁଁଥିଦେବାକେ ବି ମନା ନାଇଁ।

[Soft Outro - Both Voices, Tender Close Harmony]
ତୋର୍ ସପନ୍‌କେ ମୋର୍ ସପନ୍‌ନେ...
ଗୁଁଥିଦେବାକେ ବି ମନା ନାଇଁ।
entries.style: Sambalpuri folk ballad, gently lilting and unhurried, bamboo-flute replies over lightly played dhol, soft bass and quiet acoustic guitar; instruments sustain through clear breaths between gathering phrases and a fuller pause after the potter declaration. The bridge opens warmly without speeding up, the refrain blooms into quiet communal joy, and the duet outro settles tenderly. Warm youthful male lead with natural Sambalpuri pronunciation, compact word endings and short connected melodic turns; soft, smiling female answers from the opening, affectionate teasing and playful conversational exchanges through the verses. Female solo for the mountain-and-moon invitation; tender close-harmony duet in the final refrain and outro. Keep the pace calm and soulful; playfulness comes from vocal expression. Replies stay clear of the lead, using only supplied lyric words.

Intended reference-cover settings; verify in Suno before submission.
Policy: production/i-am-free-to-dream/settings.json @ 2026-09-27-2

model: v6
mode: Advanced
weirdness: 30
style_influence: 65
max_mode: On
personalize: Off
variety: Normal
duration: Auto
vocal_gender: Unselected; voice directed in the language prompt
audio_influence: 75
exclude_styles: EDM, heavy dance beats, aggressive percussion, theatrical belting, excessive vocal runs, vocoder, chopped vocals

For an author-approved reference cover only: audio_influence 75. Attach the exact reference and preserve its approved prompt/lyrics.
Record any author-approved settings exception in the run.

Use the existing arranged lyric for comparison. Keep its words, section order and pauses intact; log any later wording changes separately.

Start with the [shared generation baseline](../../../guides/generation-settings.md), then apply documented language or arrangement overrides. Preserve this language’s musical direction and listening checks. Explain each changed control, its musical reason and review status; record the actual settings with the take.

For the listening review:

1. Ask a fluent speaker to read the opening, gathering line, potter declaration and longest phrase naturally. Compare that phrasing with the sung version.
2. Check that the local vocal cadence and melodic treatment are audible, and that the regional character comes through beyond instrument names. Let Sambalpuri speech cadence shape short melodic turns; keep compact word endings clear and the refrain gently buoyant.
3. Check the gathering breath and fuller potter pause. Listen for dropped syllables, added words, distorted pronunciation or an accompaniment that forces a sentence to hurry.
4. Compare the opening, bridge and ending at similar playback volume. The arrangement may grow warmer, but should remain calm, soulful and quietly happy.

Keep the current translation review status until a fluent speaker and singer have reviewed the actual wording and take.
